title: Anupam Kher Just Started Shooting His 552nd Film. It's Called Shri Ram Bhoomi, and Khosla Ka Ghosla 2 Is Next.
excerpt: The veteran actor is filming a drama about Ayodhya with The Kerala Story 2 director, while simultaneously preparing to reprise his iconic role as Kamal Kishore Khosla in a long-awaited sequel.
body:
At 71, most actors would be slowing down. Anupam Kher is adding two films to his slate in the same week.

The veteran actor has officially commenced shooting for Shri Ram Bhoomi, a drama produced by Zee Studios, Dancing Shiva Films, and Cinekorn Entertainment. It marks Kher's 552nd film — a number so large it deserves its own category in Indian cinema history. The film is directed by Kamakhaya Narayan Singh, the National Award-winning filmmaker who most recently helmed The Kerala Story 2.

While the makers have kept specific plot details tightly under wraps, the title alone has set off widespread speculation. "Shri Ram Bhoomi" — literally, "the land of Lord Ram" — points directly at Ayodhya, one of the most culturally and politically significant sites in modern Indian history. The official description promises "an intense and compelling cinematic experience rooted in faith, sacrifice, truth, and one of the most consequential chapters in modern Indian history."

## A Director Who Doesn't Shy Away From Controversy

The choice of director is itself a statement. Kamakhaya Narayan Singh made waves with The Kerala Story, a polarizing film about religious conversion that became one of 2023's most discussed — and commercially successful — releases. His involvement suggests Shri Ram Bhoomi will not be a neutral, documentary-style retelling but rather an emotionally driven narrative with a point of view.

For Zee Studios, the project fits a growing industry trend: major studios betting on cultural and spiritual epics, riding the wave created by the upcoming ₹4,000 crore Ramayana adaptation and the continued box-office appeal of faith-driven narratives. The studio's announcement was deliberately evocative: "A title that echoes emotion. A story shrouded in intrigue."

Rising OTT star Ritwik Bhowmik joins the cast alongside the versatile Amruta Khanvilkar, giving the project a cross-generational ensemble that bridges classic Bollywood gravitas with contemporary screen appeal.

## Khosla Ka Ghosla Is Finally Getting a Sequel

As if one announcement were not enough, Kher will also reprise his beloved role as Kamal Kishore Khosla in Khosla Ka Ghosla 2. The original 2006 film — Dibakar Banerjee's directorial debut about a middle-class Delhi family fighting to reclaim their plot of land from a property scam — has become a cult classic in India and among NRI audiences.

The original's appeal lay in its specificity: it captured the anxiety, helplessness, and quiet resilience of ordinary Indians navigating a system designed to exploit them. For diaspora viewers, it was a film that reminded them of exactly the India their parents had described — the frustrating bureaucracy, the land disputes, the family rallying together when institutions failed.

Banerjee is returning to direct the sequel, which will reunite several original cast members including Boman Irani, Parvin Dabas, Ranvir Shorey, Kiran Juneja, and Tara Sharma. Ravi Kishan has been added to the cast in what is described as a crucial role.

No plot details have been released, but the fact that the entire original team is returning — 20 years after the first film — suggests this is being treated as a legacy project, not a cash-grab sequel.

## The Sooraj Barjatya Connection

Kher's dance card doesn't end there. He also has an as-yet-untitled project with Sooraj Barjatya, the filmmaker behind Hum Aapke Hain Koun, Maine Pyar Kiya, and Hum Saath-Saath Hain. The pairing carries deep personal significance: Barjatya was the fifth assistant director on Kher's debut film Saaransh (1984), which recently completed 42 years of its release.

The Kher-Barjatya collaboration brings together two figures whose careers have defined different eras of Hindi cinema but share a common thread: an unfashionable belief in sincerity as a cinematic value.

## Why It Matters for NRI Audiences

At 552 films, Anupam Kher's career is less a filmography and more a living archive of Indian cinema itself — from the art-house intensity of Saaransh to the mainstream warmth of Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge to the Hollywood pivot of Silver Linings Playbook.

For NRI viewers, he occupies a unique space: an actor who has worked across Bollywood, Hollywood, and the global stage, who has been outspoken about cultural identity, and who continues to take on roles that engage with questions about India's past, present, and spiritual foundation.

Whether Shri Ram Bhoomi will match the controversy of The Kerala Story or the warmth of Khosla Ka Ghosla remains to be seen. But at 552 films, Anupam Kher clearly has no intention of slowing down to find out.
